patent_summary: The document discloses a purification method for the herbicide tembotrione, whose product as made carries cyanide impurities: the product is dissolved in an aqueous solution obtained by mixing water with the solvents claim 1 enumerates without supplying a conjunction (acetonitrile, methanol, ethanol, dimethylformamide) and warmed, an adsorbent that the claim gives as activated carbon or diatomaceous earth is added and the solution held and hot-filtered, and the pH is then adjusted under temperature control to below 3 before cooling crystallises the purified tembotrione out of solution. Dependent claims 2 and 3 add only hydrochloric acid as the acid used to set the pH and a stirring-speed range for the crystallisation, and the annotated rollup records six examples whose reactions are predominantly recrystallisations alongside a smaller number of acylation, ester-formation and nucleophilic-substitution records, with no yield stated anywhere in the document.
novelty_claims: The abstract positions the method against cyanide impurities in the tembotrione product, stating that the cyanide impurity content, originally 1327 ppm, is reduced to below 100 ppm, on a comparison of the product before and after purification. What claim 1 positions as new is a purification rather than a synthesis: the product is dissolved and warmed, then "adding an adsorbent, then holding the temperature and carrying out hot filtration", then "adjusting, under temperature control, the pH of the aqueous solution to below 3, then cooling and crystallising the purified tembotrione out of the solution", with the solvent identity, the water content, the dissolution temperature, the hold time and the adsorbent all pulled into the independent claim rather than left to claims 2 and 3, which add only hydrochloric acid and a stirring speed. One element of claim 1 cannot be settled from the claims, and the ambiguity is in the Chinese as drafted rather than in translation: the solvents are joined by the enumeration comma in "a solution obtained by mixing acetonitrile, methanol, ethanol, dimethylformamide with water", so the claim does not say whether any one of them mixed with water satisfies it or all four together, and an explicit "or" (或) was available to the drafter and is used two lines later for "activated carbon or diatomaceous earth", which makes the difference deliberate on its face rather than a stylistic accident. The abstract's own support for the purity assertion is stated imprecisely, since it credits those ppm figures to Ames testing, which reports mutagenicity and not a cyanide concentration.
